context_markdown:
This register records known, intentional differences between the supplied printed source and the current edition. Entries are ordered by bar number; several entries apply one general convention at different passages. The images show representative locations, not necessarily every bar of a passage.

The historical cello treble convention sounds an octave below its written register. The [Bärenreiter Op.133 preface](https://www.barenreiter.co.uk/prefaces/9790006203109.pdf), p.XIV / PDF p.6, identifies mm.161–183, 209–216 and 573–581. It supports the convention; the supplied scan remains the comparison source.

The clef register comprises 13 passages derived from 25 changed clef instructions. There are 14 effective intervals because the edition changes from ordinary treble to tenor within mm.209–216. Boundaries can fall within a bar.

Bar references use the printed numbering. The short unnumbered bar after m.662 is not counted as m.663. This is a page-coverage review with targeted magnified checks, not an independent note-by-note transcription or a collation of all sources.
